title: Propagate Jira transition failures instead of returning false success
description:
## Finding

Jira status updates fetch a transition and POST it, but the POST result is converted to JSON `null` on every error. The method then fetches the issue and returns `Ok`, so a failed status mutation is indistinguishable from success. If a title update is also present, the method can partially apply one field while silently losing the other.

## Evidence

* `crates/thegn-svc/src/issue/jira.rs:485-526` resolves and submits the transition.
* The transition POST ends in `.await.unwrap_or(serde_json::Value::Null)`.
* `update_issue` then continues to title mutation and re-fetch without checking that the requested state was reached.

## Impact

Automations, UI actions, and agents can proceed on a false belief that work changed state, causing duplicate dispatch, invalid pipeline decisions, or partial external mutations.

## Acceptance criteria

* Propagate typed transition lookup and POST failures.
* Re-fetch and verify the issue reached the requested semantic state before success.
* Define partial-write behavior when a patch contains several fields: transactional where the provider permits, otherwise an explicit per-field result/idempotent retry contract.
* Preserve provider response context without unbounded/raw secret-bearing bodies.
* Test HTTP errors, empty/204 transition responses, unavailable transitions, stale transition IDs, partial title/status failure in both orders, and retry.

## Dependencies

Related to THE-126, THE-164, THE-195, and THE-319 (field-capability contract).
